A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CritiQ research. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including material relocated after the new appendix in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original human-preference prediction results, continual-pretraining benchmark results, component ablations, and criterion-evolution analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, annotation-size sensitivity, agent token usage, criterion statistics, and annotator agreement rates.

M1.justification: The criteria retrieval and evolution procedure, worker voting, Bradley-Terry scorer, and sampling method remain unchanged. Section 3.2 newly explains the existing deduplication step using normalized criterion names and a Jaccard threshold of 0.3; this does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Stack v2 Python subset, non-code OpenWebMath, Zyda-2, and the same nine downstream tasks. The added experiments retain this coverage. Specifying the AGIEval-sampled MATH subset clarifies an existing evaluation without establishing newly added task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds QuRator educational-value selection, labeled QR-Edu, to continual-pretraining comparisons in all three domains (Table 3), where v2 had only raw-model and uniform-sampling controls. It also adds DRPO to the code preference comparison (Table 6). QuRating's existing criterion comparisons in Table 1 are retained.

E3.justification: Table 2 revises the main code training/test split from 25/193 to 40/178 pairs. Sections 4 and 4.3 change the reported continual-pretraining model from Llama-3.1-3B to Llama-3.2-3B. Appendix B.2 adds a separate 168-pair test split with 30, 40, and 50 training pairs. These substantively revise or extend reported settings, without establishing that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B substantially extends the diagnostics with annotation-size sensitivity, manager/worker token profiling, criterion selection/revision/removal statistics, and individual criterion accuracy trajectories. These examine annotation dependence, resource requirements, and evolution behavior beyond v2's component ablations, aggregate distributions, voting analysis, and retained refinement examples.

E5.justification: V3 introduces quantitative inter-annotator agreement reporting in Table 11: 87.20%, 78.87%, and 82.00% for code, math, and logic. Both versions already state that Table 1 averages five experiments with different random seeds. No increased run count, confidence intervals, or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantive comparison and analysis results: QR-Edu's code average is 47.93 versus CritiQ's 53.88 (Table 3); DRPO obtains 68.99% code accuracy (Table 6); and annotation-size accuracies are 85.71%, 88.10%, and 88.69% on the new test split (Table 7). Tables 8–11 add further outcomes. Existing headline scores remain numerically unchanged; the revised setting descriptions prevent treating them as evidence of same-setting gains between versions.

T1.justification: The criterion-accuracy definition, voting expression, Bradley-Terry loss, sampling rule, and acceptance condition for criterion revisions are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The conclusion broadens the downstream performance claim from comparison with a uniformly sampled subset to comparison with baselines, consistent with the added QR-Edu results. The central contributions—mining criteria from limited human preferences and using a lightweight scorer for selection—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning multiple criteria, reflection, generalization, applicability, and overfitting remain substantively unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning domain coverage, subjective human preferences, continual rather than from-scratch pretraining, and the modest model scale. The new appendix primarily reports observations without developing new interpretations.

D1.justification: V3 specifies criterion-name deduplication and its 0.3 Jaccard threshold, identifies the AGIEval-sampled MATH subset, supplies the DRPO-generated prompt, and reports agent token consumption. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware information, and CritiQ prompts are retained. The repository address was already supplied in v2.

R1.justification: V3 adds Singla et al. (2024) for DRPO and Song et al. (2024), Code needs comments, to the cited literature. The existing references otherwise match, and the overall positioning against manually specified quality criteria and prior optimization approaches remains stable.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized grammar corrections, repairs the conclusion, standardizes the method-name typography, and revises the author/contact header. It inserts an Additional Experiments appendix and groups generated prompts into TextGrad and DRPO subsections. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the tabular presentation with new Tables 6–11 and QR-Edu rows and explanatory caption text in Table 3. It also relocates Algorithm 1 and several tables and reformats the retained refinement examples with BF/AF headers. Figures 1–3 retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: The added QuRator control strengthens downstream validation beyond v2's uniform-sampling comparison. Annotation-size sensitivity, agreement statistics, and implementation and resource details also improve evidential support and transparency. These gains are qualified by the unexplained relationship between revised code splits and base-model labels and the unchanged headline scores, leaving some experimental provenance unclear.
